title: Officials Say Passengers and Crew Stopped a Co-Pilot on a FlyDubai Flight
summary:
A FlyDubai plane flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv, Israel, had a serious emergency on Wednesday. The plane landed safely in Saudi Arabia, and the passengers later reached Israel on another plane.

Israeli officials said the co-pilot, who is the second pilot, tried to crash the plane and attacked the captain, Smit Machchhar. The flight-tracking website Flightradar24 said the plane's data appeared to show that it dropped nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds. After that, the plane sent emergency signals and turned toward Saudi Arabia.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the captain was seriously injured but still opened the cockpit door. He said this let passengers and crew overpower the attacker. Netanyahu praised the captain's "extraordinary bravery" and said he saved the lives of 174 people. The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said Machchhar is in a hospital in stable condition.

The airport in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, said the plane landed safely at 9:45 a.m. local time. Passenger Lital Shachaf said, "it was a miracle."

The passengers arrived in Tel Aviv on a replacement plane more than 10 hours later. Israeli officials said the reason for the attack is still being investigated. FlyDubai said it will pause its flights to and from Israel while the investigation takes place.
why_it_matters: It shows how a serious emergency was handled by the captain, crew and passengers, and why investigators take time to find the reason before giving answers.
